builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: TranSAGE: Automating Spatial Accelerator Generation for Large-Scale Transformer Models
summary: The method replaces manual or single-operation accelerator generation with a compiler pipeline that jointly optimizes multi-operation dataflow, partitions Transformer graphs, and lowers them to spatial accelerator RTL. Its cost is a hardware design and fabrication toolchain plus compiler integration, not a drop-in software change. It can fail because gains depend on producing and validating custom silicon and on whether the generated dataflow remains efficient for the exact target models and deployment stack.
rationale: This is hardware generator work for custom accelerators, which is outside production adoption on a 24 GB GPU or API-only infrastructure.
technique: Compiler-generated spatial accelerators for Transformer inference

claims.statement: The method replaces manual or single-operation accelerator generation with a compiler pipeline that jointly optimizes multi-operation dataflow, partitions Transformer graphs, and lowers them to spatial accelerator RTL. Its cost is a hardware design and fabrication toolchain plus compiler integration, not a drop-in software change. It can fail because gains depend on producing and validating custom silicon and on whether the generated dataflow remains efficient for the exact target models and deployment stack.
The authors report up to 2.41x higher throughput and 13.04x higher energy efficiency than commercial GPU/NPU baselines across four LLMs.
